```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)
library(corrplot)
```

# 1. Introduction

PyroScope is a forest fire data analysis project developed using R.
It explores forest fire patterns, weather conditions, fire occurrence,
and the burned area using statistical analysis and visualizations.

# 2. Load the Dataset

```{r load-data}
forest_data <- read.csv(
  "C:/Users/BHUMI/OneDrive/Documents/rpackage/forestfires.csv"
)

cat("Dataset loaded successfully!\n")
cat("Number of records:", nrow(forest_data), "\n")
cat("Number of columns:", ncol(forest_data), "\n")

head(forest_data)
```

# 3. Dataset Structure

```{r structure}
str(forest_data)
summary(forest_data)
```

# Statistical Summary

This section presents descriptive statistics for the numerical variables in the forest fire dataset.

```{r statistical-summary}
numeric_data <- forest_data %>%
  select(where(is.numeric))

statistical_summary <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(numeric_data),
  Mean = sapply(numeric_data, function(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
  Median = sapply(numeric_data, function(x) median(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
  Standard_Deviation = sapply(numeric_data, function(x) sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
  Minimum = sapply(numeric_data, function(x) min(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
  Maximum = sapply(numeric_data, function(x) max(x, na.rm = TRUE))
)

knitr::kable(
  statistical_summary,
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Descriptive Statistics of Forest Fire Variables"
)
```


# 4. Check Missing Values

```{r missing-values}
missing_values <- colSums(is.na(forest_data))

knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Column = names(missing_values),
    Missing_Values = as.integer(missing_values)
  ),
  caption = "Missing Values in Each Column"
)
```

# 5. Forest Fire Occurrences by Month

```{r monthly-count}
monthly_fires <- forest_data %>%
  count(month, name = "Fire_Count") %>%
  mutate(
    month = factor(
      month,
      levels = c("jan", "feb", "mar", "apr", "may", "jun",
                 "jul", "aug", "sep", "oct", "nov", "dec")
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(month)

knitr::kable(monthly_fires, caption = "Forest Fire Records by Month")

ggplot(monthly_fires, aes(x = month, y = Fire_Count)) +
  geom_col(fill = "darkorange") +
  labs(
    title = "Forest Fire Records by Month",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Number of Records"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# 6. Forest Fire Occurrences by Day

```{r daily-count}
daily_fires <- forest_data %>%
  count(day, name = "Fire_Count")

ggplot(daily_fires, aes(x = day, y = Fire_Count)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    title = "Forest Fire Records by Day of Week",
    x = "Day",
    y = "Number of Records"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# 7. Distribution of Burned Area

```{r burned-area}
ggplot(forest_data, aes(x = area)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "tomato", color = "white") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Forest Area Burned",
    x = "Burned Area (hectares)",
    y = "Frequency"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

summary(forest_data$area)
```

# 8. Temperature and Relative Humidity

```{r weather-analysis}
ggplot(forest_data, aes(x = temp, y = RH)) +
  geom_point(color = "darkgreen", alpha = 0.65) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "red") +
  labs(
    title = "Temperature vs Relative Humidity",
    x = "Temperature",
    y = "Relative Humidity (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# 9. Wind Speed and Temperature

```{r wind-temperature}
ggplot(forest_data, aes(x = wind, y = temp)) +
  geom_point(color = "purple", alpha = 0.65) +
  labs(
    title = "Wind Speed vs Temperature",
    x = "Wind Speed",
    y = "Temperature"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# 10. Average Weather Conditions by Month

```{r monthly-weather}
monthly_weather <- forest_data %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarise(
    Average_Temperature = mean(temp, na.rm = TRUE),
    Average_Humidity = mean(RH, na.rm = TRUE),
    Average_Wind = mean(wind, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

knitr::kable(
  monthly_weather,
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Average Weather Conditions by Month"
)
```

# 11. Correlation Analysis

```{r correlation, fig.width=8, fig.height=7}
numeric_data <- forest_data %>%
  select(where(is.numeric))

correlation_matrix <- cor(numeric_data, use = "complete.obs")

corrplot(
  correlation_matrix,
  method = "color",
  type = "upper",
  tl.cex = 0.7,
  title = "Correlation Between Numeric Variables",
  mar = c(0, 0, 2, 0)
)
```

# 12. Records with the Largest Burned Areas

```{r largest-fires}
largest_fires <- forest_data %>%
  arrange(desc(area)) %>%
  select(month, day, temp, RH, wind, area) %>%
  head(10)

knitr::kable(
  largest_fires,
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Top 10 Records by Burned Area"
)
```

# 13. Key Findings

```{r findings, results='asis'}
cat("- The dataset contains", nrow(forest_data), "forest fire records.\n\n")
cat("- It contains", ncol(forest_data), "variables for analysis.\n\n")
cat("- The burned-area distribution shows how fire sizes vary across records.\n\n")
cat("- Monthly and daily charts help compare recorded fire occurrences.\n\n")
cat("- Weather plots and correlation analysis help explore relationships between variables.\n\n")
```

# 14. Conclusion

PyroScope demonstrates how R can be used to analyze forest fire data through
data preparation, descriptive statistics, visualizations, and correlation
analysis. The results can help identify patterns in the recorded data.
However, observed relationships do not by themselves establish the causes
of forest fires or predict future events.


# Insights and Key Observations

This section presents important observations discovered through
statistical analysis of the forest fire dataset.

```{r project-insights}
# 1. Overall fire and burned-area statistics
total_records <- nrow(forest_data)
zero_area_fires <- sum(forest_data$area == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
positive_area_fires <- sum(forest_data$area > 0, na.rm = TRUE)

cat("1. DATASET OVERVIEW\n")
cat("-------------------\n")
cat("Total fire records:", total_records, "\n")
cat("Records with zero recorded burned area:", zero_area_fires, "\n")
cat("Records with positive burned area:", positive_area_fires, "\n\n")

# 2. Month with the most recorded fires
fire_by_month <- forest_data %>%
  count(month, name = "Fire_Records") %>%
  arrange(desc(Fire_Records))

cat("2. MONTHLY FIRE PATTERN\n")
cat("-----------------------\n")
cat("Month with the most recorded fire observations:",
    as.character(fire_by_month$month[1]), "\n")
cat("Number of observations in that month:",
    fire_by_month$Fire_Records[1], "\n\n")

# 3. Distribution of burned area
cat("3. BURNED-AREA DISTRIBUTION\n")
cat("---------------------------\n")
cat("Mean burned area:", round(mean(forest_data$area, na.rm = TRUE), 2), "\n")
cat("Median burned area:", round(median(forest_data$area, na.rm = TRUE), 2), "\n")
cat("Largest recorded burned area:", round(max(forest_data$area, na.rm = TRUE), 2), "\n")

if (mean(forest_data$area, na.rm = TRUE) >
    median(forest_data$area, na.rm = TRUE)) {
  cat("Observation: The mean exceeds the median, suggesting that larger fire events may influence the average.\n\n")
} else {
  cat("Observation: The mean does not exceed the median in this dataset.\n\n")
}

# 4. Weather variable correlations with burned area
cat("4. CORRELATION WITH BURNED AREA\n")
cat("--------------------------------\n")

weather_variables <- c("temp", "RH", "wind", "rain")

for (variable in weather_variables) {
  correlation_value <- cor(
    forest_data[[variable]],
    forest_data$area,
    use = "complete.obs"
  )

  cat(
    variable, "vs burned area:",
    round(correlation_value, 3), "\n"
  )
}

cat("\nNote: Correlation shows association, not proof of cause and effect.\n")
```
